title: fix: a file cannot replace an extension installed from the store
head: 58914b08a9638dd2d4e890d73ae40e8dff02bd16
body:
## What

A package installed from a file (`Tier::FromFile`) could silently replace an extension installed through the trusted store path (a reviewed third-party package), as long as its version was higher. The existing guard only protected first-party extensions.

## Why

The on-disk store is the trusted root: a reviewed third-party package was verified before it landed. A local file with the same id and a higher version must not overwrite that verification result — the person removes the store copy first if they really want the file version.

## How

- New error `StoreError::WouldReplaceStorePackage`: "this file has the same id as an extension installed from the catalogue; remove that extension first".
- New guard in `install_staged`: `tier == FromFile && existing.tier != FromFile` refuses; the existing first-party guard is unchanged, so a reviewed third-party source still cannot replace a first-party extension either.
- A file can still replace another file-installed package (version rules apply).
- Failing-first test `a_file_cannot_replace_an_extension_installed_from_the_store` injects a `ReviewedThirdParty` record via state.json (no catalogue client exists yet), asserts the refusal, that the store copy and the generation are untouched, and that uninstall makes the file installable.
- Mutation harness entry "store: a file replaces a store-installed extension" killed by the new test; store mutants now 35, all caught (32 by tests, 3 equivalent with stated reasons).
- README store row updated to the new counts.
